links.targetTitle: Operational GovOps can block the rebate surplus distribution

title: Unresolved Agent–GovOps disputes escalate to Core GovOps, moving the decision out of the Agent's own governance
content:
The rebate protocol closes with an escalation rule: "If Operational GovOps and Launch Agent 7 cannot resolve the disagreement, it must be escalated to Core GovOps" (A.6.1.1.8.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.3).

This is one of the few places in the Artifact where a deadlock is given a defined exit. The ladder has three rungs — the Agent and its Operational GovOps attempt resolution bilaterally; failing that, Core GovOps takes it; and because Core GovOps sits at ecosystem level rather than inside either party's Artifact, the final rung is outside the dispute.

Escalation is mandatory ("must be escalated"), not permissive. Neither side can choose stalemate as an outcome, which matters because stalemate is not neutral here: an unresolved dispute means the distribution stays blocked indefinitely and the Agent's token holders bear the cost of the delay.

What the text does not supply is the other half of a dispute mechanism — no deadline for declaring irresolution, no standard Core GovOps applies, and no statement that its determination binds. The route out exists; its terms are specified elsewhere or not yet.

The structural point stands regardless: Agent-level governance is not the last word even on the Agent's own money, which is consistent with the Artifact's general subordination of Agent authority to the ecosystem.
description: The Artifact defines a two-tier ladder with a terminal step at ecosystem level, so a deadlock between an Agent and its Executor cannot simply persist unresolved.
